steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Narrative perspective: 1st (intimate, biased), 3rd limited (one consciousness), omniscient (all-knowing), stream of consciousness

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Setting: time, place, atmosphere; pathetic fallacy; symbolic settings

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Themes: developed through motifs, recurring images, contrasts, parallels

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Discuss how the first-person narration in 'The Great Gatsby' shapes our understanding of Gatsby --- Solution: Nick as participant-observer creates intimacy but limits access to Gatsby's interiority. His judgement 'Gatsby turned out all right' frames our view. Unreliable moments (drunk at party) and admiration create ambivalence. We see Gatsby through Nick's romanticisation
